intended_object: The object part of the left adjoint L to the comparison functor K : D → T-Alg (T = GF) in Beck's monadicity theorem: an algebra (A, a) goes to the coequalizer in D of F a, ε_{FA} : FGFA ⇉ FA. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the file (Monadicity.lean).
explanation: For an algebra A of the monad GF, A.a : G(F A.A) → A.A, so F.map A.a : FGF A.A → F A.A. The counit component adj.counit.app (F A.A) has the same source and target. The definition returns the coequalizer of these two maps, which is exactly the textbook construction (Mac Lane VI.7; Riehl). It assumes only that this one coequalizer exists, the minimal hypothesis. The setting (arbitrary categories with an adjunction F ⊣ G) is the natural one; the shared morphism universe v₁ follows the file's conventions and does not change the mathematics. The definition sits in a proof-internal namespace, but it is still the standard, named construction from the proof of Beck's theorem, so I judge it faithful.
